children: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $402.7 million, up 1% from $398.7 million a year earlier, while its net loss attributable to common shareholders widened to $63.1 million, or $0.56 per diluted share, primarily reflecting a higher impairment charge. Results exceeded management’s outlook as demand and pricing improved, partly offset by lower revenue from non-comparable properties.
Revenue was $402.7M, compared with $398.7M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 1.0%.
Net income attributable to common shareholders was $(63.1)M, compared with $(43.4)M in the prior-year quarter.
Diluted EPS was $(0.56), compared with $(0.37) in the prior-year quarter.
Same-property RevPAR rose 8.3% to $256.66, with occupancy increasing to 80.6% and average daily rate reaching $318.52.
Resorts led portfolio growth, while urban hotels also performed well, particularly in San Francisco, Chicago, Los Angeles, Boston and Washington, D.C.
Nine-month revenue increased $29.0 million, supported by stronger average daily rates, recovering Los Angeles demand and San Francisco business travel.
Efficiency initiatives and out-of-room spending supported profitability. Management plans $60 million to $70 million in property upgrades in 2026.
